questions.stem: The Himalayas are divided into three main parallel ranges from north to south. Which range is the HIGHEST and contains Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas have three longitudinal divisions (from N to S): (1) GREATER HIMALAYAS (Himadri/Inner/Central) — tallest, contains Everest (8,848m), Kanchenjunga (8586m — 3rd highest), Makalu, Cho Oyu, Dhaulagiri; perennial snow; source of major rivers. (2) LESSER HIMALAYAS (Himachal/Middle) — ranges like Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mussoorie, Nag Tibba, Mahabharat; hill stations (Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital, Darjeeling); avg 3500-5000m. (3) SHIVALIK (Outer/Sub-Himalayas) — 900-1200m, youngest range; covered with dense forests; famous for Siwalik fossils. TRANS-HIMALAYAS (Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar) lie NORTH of the Greater Himalayas — K2 (8611m — 2nd highest globally) is in Karakoram.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which is India's HIGHEST mountain peak (in Indian territory)?
questions.explanation: KANCHENJUNGA (8,586m, Sikkim) is India's highest peak within undisputed Indian territory — also the world's 3rd highest mountain after Everest and K2. MOUNT EVEREST (8848m) is on the Nepal-Tibet (China) border, NOT Indian. K2 (8611m, world's 2nd highest) is in the Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir region (disputed but claimed by both India and Pakistan; practically accessed via Pakistan) — NOT counted as Indian by most authorities. NANDA DEVI (7816m, Uttarakhand) is the 2nd-highest peak within India's actual jurisdiction. Kanchenjunga is sacred to Sikkimese Buddhists — climbers traditionally stop just short of the summit as a mark of respect.

questions.stem: Which Himalayan pass connects Srinagar with Leh and remains closed for 4-6 months in winter?
questions.explanation: ZOJI LA (3528m) in Ladakh connects Srinagar (Kashmir Valley) to Leh via Kargil — the critical road link for Ladakh, closed by snow Dec-May. ZOJILA TUNNEL (under construction as of 2024, India's longest road tunnel at 14.1 km) will make it all-weather. Other key Himalayan passes: BANIHAL (Jawahar Tunnel, Jammu-Srinagar); ROHTANG (Manali-Leh, HP — also being replaced by Atal Tunnel since 2020, 9 km, world's longest at 10000ft altitude); KHARDUNG LA (Leh-Nubra, was claimed 'world's highest motorable' at 5359m — now superseded by Umling La, Ladakh at 5883m — world's highest motorable road since 2021); CHANG LA (Leh-Pangong); NATHULA (Sikkim-Tibet, trade); JELEP LA (Sikkim); BOMDILA + BUM LA (Arunachal-Tibet); LIPULEKH (Uttarakhand-Tibet, pilgrimage to Kailash); SHIPKI LA (HP-Tibet, Sutlej).

questions.stem: The Siachen Glacier, known as the world's highest battlefield, is located in which region?
questions.explanation: SIACHEN GLACIER (~76 km long, 2nd longest non-polar glacier after Fedchenko in Tajikistan) lies in the Karakoram Range of eastern Ladakh, between the Saltoro Ridge (west) and the main Karakoram (east). India took control of the entire glacier on 13 April 1984 via OPERATION MEGHDOOT (launched by Lt Gen M. L. Chibber + Colonel Narinder 'Bull' Kumar), pre-empting a planned Pakistani occupation. Average altitude ~5400m; temperatures as low as −60°C. The tri-junction of India, Pakistan and China is nearby (Indira Col). Longest glacier system entirely in India: GANGOTRI (30 km, Uttarakhand — source of Bhagirathi-Ganga). India controlled since Operation Meghdoot, 1984.
questions.subject: Geography

_fixes.was: Karakoram Range, Ladakh (India controlled since Operation Meghdoot, 1984)

questions.stem: Nathula Pass, a key India-China trade route at 4310 m in the Eastern Himalayas, is in which state?
questions.explanation: NATHULA PASS (4310m) is in Sikkim, on the India-China (Tibet) border, part of the ancient Silk Route branch connecting Lhasa to Kolkata via Kalimpong. Closed after the 1962 Sino-Indian war; REOPENED in 2006 for trade. The area saw Chinese incursions in 1967 (Nathu La clashes — Indian army repulsed). Open for tourists from Indian side May-November. Nearby: JELEP LA (4267m, historically more important than Nathula) — also in Sikkim. DOKLAM plateau (tri-junction India-Bhutan-China) lies south of Nathula — site of 2017 India-China standoff.

questions.stem: The Karakoram Pass, historically a key trade route between India (Leh) and Yarkand (China's Xinjiang), lies in which state/UT?
questions.explanation: KARAKORAM PASS (5540m), in the Ladakh UT on the India-China border, is one of the highest passes in the world — named the 'Pass of Black Gravel'. Historically part of the Silk Route linking Leh to Kashgar and Yarkand. Now closed for civilian crossing; lies near the Siachen region. Other Ladakh/J&K passes: SASER LA, KHARDUNG LA, CHANG LA, MARSIMIK LA, PEMZAL LA. Umling La (5883m, Ladakh) became the world's highest motorable in 2021 (BRO built). Main Karakoram range features K2 (8611m), Gasherbrum I & II, Broad Peak (all in Pak-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT among India's 10+ 7000-metre-plus peaks (in Indian-administered territory)?
questions.explanation: ANNAPURNA I (8091m — world's 10th highest) is in NEPAL, not India. India's key 7000m+ peaks in undisputed territory: KANCHENJUNGA (8586m, Sikkim — highest in India), NANDA DEVI (7816m, Uttarakhand), KAMET (7756m, Uttarakhand), SALTORO KANGRI (7742m, Ladakh), SASER KANGRI (7672m, Ladakh), MAMOSTONG KANGRI (7516m, Ladakh), MANA (7272m, UK), CHAUKHAMBA (7138m, UK), TRISUL (7120m, UK), KEDARNATH (6940m, UK). India's high peaks concentrate in the Karakoram (Ladakh), Kumaon-Garhwal (Uttarakhand), and Sikkim Himalayas. Himachal's highest: Reo Purgyil (6816m).

questions.stem: The Himalayan river system has THREE major rivers originating from Tibet/Himalayas. Which one rises in the TIBETAN PLATEAU and is known there as 'Yarlung Tsangpo'?
questions.explanation: BRAHMAPUTRA rises near Lake Manasarovar (Tibet) as the Yarlung Tsangpo, flows EAST across southern Tibet for ~1700 km, takes a sharp 'Great Bend' around Namcha Barwa, then enters Arunachal Pradesh as the SIANG / DIHANG. Joined by Lohit and Dibang at Sadiya → becomes the BRAHMAPUTRA flowing west through Assam. Enters Bangladesh as JAMUNA, merges with Padma (Ganga) and Meghna before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. INDUS also rises near Manasarovar, flows NW into Ladakh and then PoK. GANGA rises as Bhagirathi from Gangotri Glacier (UK), joined by Alaknanda at Devprayag to officially become the Ganga. Yamuna rises at Yamunotri (UK).

questions.stem: The flat-bottomed, fertile longitudinal valleys found between the Shivalik Hills and the Lesser Himalayas are locally known as what?

options.option_text: Duns — alluvial-floored valleys like Dehradun and Patli Dun
Karewas — ancient lacustrine terraces found in Kashmir valley
Bugyals — high-altitude alpine meadows used for seasonal grazing
Bhabar — coarse gravel belt at the base of Himalayan foothills

questions.explanation: Duns are flat-floored synclinal valleys between the Shivaliks and Lesser Himalayas, formed by alluvial deposition — Dehradun and Patli Dun are the most famous. Bugyals are high-altitude meadows in the Greater Himalayas used for transhumance. Karewas are Kashmir-specific lacustrine deposits, and Bhabar is the coarse gravel zone just south of the Shivaliks — none of these describes inter-range longitudinal valleys.

questions.stem: Kashmir's world-famous GI-tagged Kesar (saffron) is cultivated primarily on which type of elevated soil deposit unique to the region?

options.option_text: Bhabar — coarse gravel-based soils at the Himalayan foot slopes
Karewas — flat-topped elevated terraces of ancient lacustrine origin
Terai — waterlogged marshy soils south of the Shivalik range
Regur — black cotton soil derived from the Deccan Trap volcanics

questions.explanation: Karewas are flat-topped elevated terraces formed from ancient glacial and lacustrine deposits in the Kashmir valley. Their well-drained, fine-textured soil — typically at 1500–1800 m — provides ideal conditions for saffron cultivation, which holds a GI tag. Bhabar and Terai are features of the Himalayan foothill zone, while Regur (black soil) is restricted to the Deccan plateau — none suits the Kashmir valley.

questions.stem: Rivers like the Indus, Sutlej, and Brahmaputra are termed 'antecedent rivers' because they predated the Himalayan uplift and maintained their courses by cutting gorges as the mountains rose. Which of the following is NOT an antecedent river?

options.option_text: Indus — rises near Mansarovar and predates the Himalayan ranges
Sutlej — originates from Rakas Tal in Tibet and cuts through ranges
Brahmaputra — originates in Tibet as Yarlung Tsangpo, older than ranges
Ganga — a consequent river formed from Himalayan glaciers after uplift

questions.explanation: The Ganga (Bhagirathi/Alaknanda system) is a consequent river — it formed after the Himalayas rose, flowing along the slope gradient. In contrast, Indus, Sutlej, and Brahmaputra are antecedent rivers that existed before the Himalayan uplift and carved deep gorges as the mountains rose around them. A common student error is assuming any river 'from the Himalayas' is antecedent; antecedence refers specifically to pre-tectonic origin.

questions.stem: Lipulekh Pass in Uttarakhand's Pithoragarh district — historically used for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra — sits at the tri-junction of India, China (Tibet), and which third country that released a controversial revised map claiming this area in 2020?

options.option_text: Bhutan — which disputes the Doklam plateau with India and China
Nepal — whose 2020 revised map claimed Kalapani and Lipulekh area
Myanmar — which shares the northeastern Himalayan border with India
Pakistan — which disputes the Siachen and Aksai Chin border areas

questions.explanation: Lipulekh sits at the tri-junction of India, Nepal, and China (Tibet). The Kalapani area — where the Kali river (Mahakali) originates — has been disputed between India and Nepal. In May 2020, Nepal published a revised political map claiming Lipulekh, Kalapani, and Limpiyadhura as its territory. Bhutan's dispute (Doklam) is in the eastern Himalayas; Pakistan and Myanmar have no proximity to this Uttarakhand pass.

questions.stem: In Himalayan geology, the 'Main Central Thrust' (MCT) is a major fault zone. Which tectonic boundary does it mark?

options.option_text: Suture zone where the Indian plate underthrusts the Eurasian plate
Fault separating the Lesser Himalayas from the Siwalik (Outer) Hills
Boundary separating the Higher (Greater) Himalayas from the Lesser Himalayas
Lineament marking the Precambrian shield boundary south of the ranges

questions.explanation: The Himalayan thrust system has three main faults north to south: Main Central Thrust (MCT) separates the Greater Himalayas from the Lesser Himalayas; Main Boundary Thrust (MBT) separates the Lesser Himalayas from the Siwaliks; Himalayan Frontal Thrust (HFT) marks the Siwalik–plains boundary. The Indus-Tsangpo Suture Zone — not MCT — marks where the Indian and Eurasian plates collided. Students frequently swap MCT with MBT.

questions.stem: The Valley of Flowers National Park in Uttarakhand — co-inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site along with Nanda Devi National Park — is situated in the valley of which river?

options.option_text: Mandakini river — flowing through the Kedarnath wildlife sanctuary
Pindar river — draining the Bageshwar and Chamoli district area
Pushpawati river — a tributary of Alaknanda in the Bhyundar valley
Bhagirathi river — which drains the Gangotri glacier and Gaumukh

questions.explanation: The Valley of Flowers lies in the Bhyundar valley of Chamoli district, through which the Pushpawati river (a tributary of the Alaknanda) flows. Declared a National Park in 1982 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988, it is renowned for endemic alpine flora. Students commonly guess Mandakini (Kedarnath area) or Bhagirathi (Gangotri area) as these are better-known Uttarakhand Himalayan river valleys, but neither passes through the Bhyundar valley.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly pairs a trans-Himalayan river with its actual source on the Tibetan plateau?

options.option_text: Indus — originates from Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh (India)
Kali/Sharda — originates from Mansarovar lake in Tibet
Brahmaputra — originates from Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand
Sutlej — originates from Rakas Tal (Rakshas Tal) lake in Tibet

questions.explanation: The Sutlej correctly originates from Rakas Tal (Rakshas Tal) in Tibet, near Lake Mansarovar. The Indus rises from Sengge Khabab ('Lion's Mouth') spring near Mansarovar in Tibet — not from Rohtang Pass. The Kali/Sharda river originates from Kalapani spring near Lipulekh in Uttarakhand, not from Mansarovar. The Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo) rises from the Angsi glacier in Tibet — not from Gangotri. These cross-pairings are among the most common source-confusion errors in exam preparation.
